newsitem.title: SPAIN: EU Mideast envoy proposes new peace initiative.
newsitem.headline: EU Mideast envoy proposes new peace initiative.

text.p: The European Union has proposed the creation of a new permanent Israeli-Palestinian security committee in a bid to salvage the stalled Middle East peace process, an EU envoy said on Monday.

"The European Union is seeking to present some concrete ideas for the creation of a permanent security committee in which Israelis and Palestinians work together continuously and not on an interim basis," EU Middle East envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos told Spanish state television.

Moratinos spoke after meeting Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Jerusalem to try to avert a collapse of the peace process after Palestinian suicide bombers killed 13 people and wounded 170 in an Israeli market last week.
The committee could bring Israeli and Palestinian security authorities together to exchange information, the former Spanish ambassador to Israel said.

The Oslo peace accords already provide for a joint Israeli-Palestinian security liaison committee but cooperation between the two sides has steadily broken down since March when the right-wing Israeli government launched a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Moratinos said he had asked Netanyahu, at the request of Arafat, to ease punitive measures against Palestinians taken after the bombing in Jewish West Jerusalem's main open-air produce market.

Israel has suspended peace talks with the Palestinians, rounded up scores of suspected militants, closed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, demanded the extradition of the PLO police chief and threatened to re-enter Palestinian self-rule areas to seize militants if Arafat failed to do the job.
His office said in a statement after the meeting that the government was trying to "pressure the Palestinian Authority to fulfil its obligations".
Moratinos said Netanyahu had assured him he was willing to ease the measures once Arafat had taken stronger action to eradicate the sources of violence and to prevent further attacks on Israelis.
